newsitem.title: USA: IMF unlikely to reach quota pact in April-Maystadt.
newsitem.headline: IMF unlikely to reach quota pact in April-Maystadt.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is unlikely to reach agreement on a plan to boost its resources at its semi-annual meeting here next month, the head of the IMF's policy-making Interim Committee said on Monday.
"I don't expect a decision at the next meeting," Philippe Maystadt, who is also Belgian Finance Minister, told reporters.
He voiced hopes though that some progress will be made on the issue at the Committee's meeting in late April.
The vast majority of the IMF's member nations have already made clear that they are willing to back a significant increase in the Fund's resources, or quotas.
But U.S. President Bill Clinton's administration, wary of the Congressional response to a new request for money for the IMF, has so far stopped short of signalling its acceptance.
"I can guess that the other members of the Interim Committee won't be particularly happy if they have to wait for the decision of the United States," Maystadt said.
But he argued that what was important was the result.
If the Clinton administration believes it has more of a chance of winning Congressional approval of an IMF quota increase by waiting and grouping it with other requests, that is its decision to make.
